identity.name: Pigeon Lake
identity.summary: Large shallow prairie/parkland lake. Rideable days are driven mainly by synoptic/frontal wind; lake breeze is a modest secondary enhancer. No gap/venturi.

geometry.notes: Enough fetch for organized open-water wind and chop; shoreline trees/cottages create nearshore junk wind and local shadows.

windRegime.directionNotes: Usable from most directions if you pick the matching shore. NW/W common on post-frontal/synoptic days; S/SE/SW also used (esp. snowkite launches). Beach selection matters more than a single 'best direction'.

seasonality.spring: Often best for synoptic gradients; cold water; shoulder season windiest useful period with fall.
seasonality.summer: More light days; lake breeze relatively more important; convective gusts/storm outflows possible.
seasonality.fall: Strong synoptic setups return; cooling lake can sharpen thermal contrast on sunny days.
seasonality.winter: Snowkite on ice when safe; open-water sports iced out. Strong winds still occur over ice.

proxyPoints.description: Central open-water cell approximating mid-lake wind without shoreline roughness.
NW of lake over land/parkland—useful when flow is NW to check regional background before lake modification.
SW approach proxy for SW/W synoptic and diluted chinook-influenced regimes.

ridePoints.name: Ma-Me-O Beach
ridePoints.notes: Popular SE-shore public beach/day-use area. Best with northerly component and fetch across the lake. Confirm local access/rules.

ridePoints.name: Pigeon Lake Provincial Park (east side area)
ridePoints.notes: Park access/parking; prefer westerlies with open fetch. Exact launch depends on facilities and regulations.

ridePoints.name: North shore launches (generic)
ridePoints.notes: Used when wind is from the south sector (including some snowkite ops). Multiple private/cottage accesses—treat as directional class, not a single pin.

enhancerModel.description: On sunny days with weak–moderate synoptic wind, expect a modest afternoon lake-breeze boost and more onshore component at heated shores. Do NOT use La Ventana +8 mph constants.

rulesSeed.notes: Seed guesses only. Calibrate against buoy + rider reports. Likely much weaker than coastal desert thermals.

enhancerModel.triggerLogic: If afternoon solar is high AND synoptic background is light-moderate, add small onshore-biased boost at sun-exposed shores. If synoptic already strong (>~15–18 kt), thermal add-on is secondary; prefer raw background + gust factor.

cloudSensitivity.notes: Cloud mainly affects the weak lake-breeze component. Strong frontal days can still blow under overcast. Thunderstorm outflow days are hazardous exceptions.

failureModes.description: Launching in the lee of forested shoreline or in tight bays → light, holey, directionally messy wind while mid-lake is better.
Lake is multidirectional; bad shore choice kills the session even when regional wind is good.
Quiet summer ridging with little pressure gradient → unrideable despite sunshine; lake breeze alone often insufficient for kiters needing 12+ kt.
Thunderstorm gust fronts: short violent spikes, rapid lulls, dangerous for beginners.
Cold unstable NW flow can be very gusty—usable but harder for learners.
Buildings/docks/trees create junk wind at the beach even when buoy shows clean mid-lake flow.
Freeze-up / breakup: changing surface, access, and verification; snowkite ice safety critical.
Occasional warmer W/SW regimes with mountain-lee influence aloft; usually not a true chinook jet at this latitude/distance, but can change temp, stability, and gustiness.

stations.name: Pigeon Lake Watershed Association central basin buoy
stations.notes: Best on-lake truth for open-water season. Represents open-water zone, not beach roughness.

nearbyReferences.description: Edmonton-area airport METARs for synoptic pattern cross-check (not lake-specific).

riderReports.suggestedPrompt: Was it rideable 1–5pm at your beach? Avg wind feel? Gusty? Which shore?

rideableThresholdsKt.notes: Seed thresholds for large light-wind kiters common on AB lakes (often 14–16m). Tune with local gear norms.

forecastBands.inspiredBy: MasViento range convention adapted to knots

steps: Fetch multi-model wind at open_lake_center and upstream proxies
Classify regime: frontal/synoptic vs light-thermal candidate
Apply small thermal add-on only if eligible; else use background
Map direction to recommended shores / warn lee launches
Score confidence from model agreement + buoy availability
Emit Forecast Object then rider brief

confidenceHeuristics.high: Models agree within ~3 kt and direction sector; buoy trend matches; clear synoptic driver
confidenceHeuristics.medium: Models agree on direction but speed spread >3–5 kt; or thermal day with uncertain sun
confidenceHeuristics.low: Light/variable; pre-frontal wind shift timing; convection possible; ice transition

dataSourcesSuggested: Open-Meteo multi-model (ECMWF, ICON, GFS, Canadian models if available)
Environment Canada / regional warnings for severe convection
Optional: webcam or parking activity as weak proxy later

nextActions: Log 20–40 sessions against buoy + beach reports
Confirm preferred launches per 8-point wind rose with locals
Separate open-water vs snowkite seasonal profiles if needed

analogSpots.name: Wabamun Lake
analogSpots.why: Nearby AB lake, similar synoptic driver; different shoreline hazards (power plant/ice).

analogSpots.name: Other central Alberta recreational lakes
analogSpots.why: Same regime class: synoptic primary, weak lake breeze, fetch/shore selection critical.

safetyNotes: Shallow areas and recreational boat traffic in summer
Cold water most of season—exposure risk
Thunderstorm season: do not treat outflow as a planned window
Snowkite: ice thickness/safety is rider responsibility; never trust forecasts for ice
